entry.dc:title: SURVIVAL STRATEGY: EVERY BIT COUNTS.
entry.dc:creator: Garg O.
entry.dc:description: The Iron Ore Company of Canada (IOC) operations in Labrador and Quebec among the largest open-pit mining complexes on a world basis. Since the 1981-82 recession, IOC has embarked on a cost reduction and productivity improvement program in order to survive in the world iron ore market. This paper outlines the approach used in prioritizing the cost reduction items.

entry.dc:title: Considerations Concerning the Effect of the Grain Size of Blasted Material on Hard-Rock Open-Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Lechner E.
entry.dc:description: The character of blasted material with respect to its grain size can properly be demonstrated by its grading curve on the RRS-diagram. For different grading curves the quantity of boulders and the relative digging resistance are investigated as functions of the bucket capacity. These results form the fundamentals for determining the character of the blasted material with respect to its loading properties. Subsequently the connection between the character of the blasted rock and the production capacity, as well as the cost for the hydraulic shovel and track system, is investigated. Blasted material of poor character leads to significant increases in cost.

entry.dc:title: IN-THE-WALL HAULAGE FOR OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Hustrulid W.A.
entry.dc:description: As open pits become deeper and ore grades become lower, there is a great need for innovation in surface mining. A suggestion made by Henriksson in the early 1970s was for the consideration of in-the-wall haulage systems in conjunction with or in place of the conventional in-the-pit ramp system. Since then, few, if any, mines have adopted such a system. This paper has reexamined the concept and attempted to describe some reasons why mine planners might consider it in the future. The authors believe there are ore bodies/ pits for which this method should be strongly considered. A combination of an in-the-wall haulage system with a program of rock reinforcement and ground water depressurization would be a major innovation in mining because pit slopes could possibly be safely steepened from the conventional 40 degree -50 degree to 60 degree -70 degree . This could save millions of tons of stripping.

entry.dc:title: SETTLEMENT INSTRUMENTATION TO OBSERVE OPEN-PIT MINE BACKFILL AND A PROTOTYPE FOUNDATION IN WESTERN CANADA.
entry.dc:creator: Thomson S.
entry.dc:description: The settlement of the spoil from one open-pit mining operation west of Edmonton, Alberta, was monitored by a series of magnetic extensometers installed in boreholes. Time-settlement plots indicated that self-weight settlement occurs within a 3-5 year period. Tests of individual small footings pointed out the necessity of placing shallow foundations on beneficiated soil. The results of a second series of small footings led to the founding of an 8 multiplied by 10 m prototype instrumented, reinforced foundation on a 1 m thick soil - flyash mat. Observations to date indicate an entirely acceptable settlement pattern.

entry.dc:title: THE LONG‐TERM EFFECTS OF A TOKEN ECONOMY ON SAFETY PERFORMANCE IN OPEN‐PIT MINING
entry.dc:creator: Fox D.K.
entry.dc:description: A token economy that used trading stamps as tokens was instituted at two dangerous open‐pit mines. Employees earned stamps for working without lost‐time injuries, for being in work groups in which all other workers had no lost‐time injuries, for not being involved in equipment‐damaging accidents, for making adopted safety suggestions, and for unusual behavior which prevented an injury or accident. They lost stamp awards if they or other workers in their group were injured, caused equipment damage, or failed to report accidents or injuries. The stamps could be exchanged for a selection of thousands of items at redemption stores. Implementation of the token economy was followed by large reductions in the number of days lost from work because of injuries, the number of lost‐time injuries, and the costs of accidents and injuries. The reductions in costs far exceeded the costs of operating the token economy. All improvements were maintained over several years. 1987 Society for the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

entry.dc:title: CRITERIA FOR THE MATERIAL SELECTION FOR AIRCRAFT STRUCTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Iron and Steel Institute of Japan
entry.dc:description: A comparison of numerical evaluations of the H. K. Taylor and Zwiagin formula with the use of data from underground coal mines shows that the former predicts higher optimum output levels for reserves in excess of about 60,000,000t. For smaller reserves the two methods are more or less comparable. When applied to open-bit lignite mines with reserves of 20,000,000-160,000,000t it appears that the upper limit of the Taylor relation provides a better approximation of optimum output than the usual formulation. This is explained by the facts that in open-pit mining it is possible to use highly efficient mining equipment, transport facilities are more flexible and better working conditions reduce the accident rate. The data are based on a mine in Turkey.

entry.dc:title: BASIC STAGES IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF ELECTRIC LOCOMOTIVE PRODUCTION AT THE NOVOCHERKASSKY ELECTRIC LOCOMOTIVE PLANT.
entry.dc:creator: Duvarov V.
entry.dc:description: The Novocherkassky Electric Locomotive Plant (NEVZ) is a major enterprise in the field of heavy transportation machinery construction with an electrical equipment profile. The Plant is now turning out mainline (road) ac freight locomotives, diesel-electric traction units for open-pit mining operations, vehicles for the Toilisi Electric Locomotive Plant (TEVZ), and motors for the Dnepropetrovskii Electric Locomotive Plant (DEVZ). More than 80% of the freight moving over the electrified mainline railways of the USSR is hauled by locomotives manufactured at the NEVZ. The history of the Plant is recalled and the main stages in its development are described. Recently, the development of a new generation of twelve-axle two-section electric locomotives has commenced on the basis of the VL85 locomotive.

entry.dc:title: ADVANCES IN OVERBURDEN BLAST-CASTING.
entry.dc:creator: Gupta R.N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The paper presents an overview of the global development in the field of overburden blast-casting. Parameters to be considered for a successful casting of overburden by blasting are discussed. The economical and environmental aspects of explosive casting are detailed. In India, where more than 60% of coal production is expected from opencast method, blast-casting is anticipated to be a cheaper alternative to conventional stripping operations. For open-pit mining of developed coal seams in Indian coalfields, blast-casting is likely to offer special technological advantages.

entry.dc:title: DESIGN AND CALCULATION FOR A SLURRY EXPLOSIVE CHARGING VEHICLE.
entry.dc:creator: Sun Z.
entry.prism:publicationName: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
entry.dc:description: In China, a variety of industrial explosives are being rapidly developed. The slurry explosive is one of the major blasting agents used in open-pit mining. Nevertheless, its charging technology is rather primitive. This paper offers a systematic description of a slurry explosive charging machine, as well as its design and calculation.

entry.dc:title: Computer-Aided Planning of an Open-Pit Mine in Unconsolidated Rock.
entry.dc:creator: Moser M.
entry.dc:description: The solution of certain planning tasks connected with open-pit mining in unconsolidated rock is not only made easier by the computer but in some cases only first becomes possible with the aid of the computer. In order to be able to execute the large mass movements of this type of operation at low cost, the crucial points of the planning, such as winning and the depositing of waste in the course of regular operation, are optimized with the aid of a computer on the basis of a planning example, and the operations required are discussed. The presentation of the results of seven essential working steps makes it possible to evaluate the quality of computer-aided planning of open-pit mining.

entry.dc:title: GOLDEN GLOW AT BATTLE MOUNTAIN.
entry.dc:creator: Argall G.
entry.dc:description: By all standards, Nevada's Battle Mountain Gold Co. (BMG) is a rare species as a mining company. Hatched December 1984 as a spin-off vehicle by a parent oil company disenchanted with the mining industry, BMG was literally born with a gold bar in its treasury. As of January 1, 1985, measured and indicated gold and silver reserves were 7,723,000 st assaying 0. 154 tr oz/st gold and 0. 831 tr oz/st silver in the main orebody - the Fortitude. The nearby Northwest Extension orebody has 693,000 st of demonstrated reserves assaying 0. 102 tr oz/st gold and 0. 346 tr oz/st silver. In addition to the precious metals reserves, BMG inherited (all but free of short and long-term debt) a 50,000-st/d open-pit mining fleet; a 3,600-st/d-capacity grinding/cyanidation/carbon-in-pulp milling plant; spare equipment inventories; mine buildings; and all other facilities to support the operation. All Battle Mountain mining claims and interests in several exploration projects were included.

entry.dc:title: Seismic attenuation spectra in rock mass characterization: a case study in open-pit mining.
entry.dc:creator: Young R.P.
entry.dc:description: The application of engineering geophysics to the characterization of rock masses is exemplified through a case study of 3 phases of a research project into the design of efficient blasting systems in open-pit mining. Seismic experiments are used before and after in blasting to monitor the efficiency of explosions in terms of rock fragmentation. Spectral analysis of seismic signals, after they have been used to interrogate rock masses, is used to compute preblast and postblast attenuation and velocity parameters. The results show that fragmentation efficiency of a mine blast and fracture anisotropy of a rock mass can be quantified in terms of 3-D attenuation spectra and polar anisotropy diagrams.-from Authors

entry.dc:title: Modeling the explosion of a system of borehole charges in a scarp
entry.dc:creator: Neiman I.B.
entry.dc:description: On the basis of the mathematical model here proposed for the action of the explosion of two cylindrical (borehole) explosive charges in the scarp of a rock mass, the scope for investigating the correlation between wave propagation parameters with scarp rock cutting in a pit is expanded. This offers the possibility of solving a series of problem associated with the correction of wave propagation parameters and their optimization in conditions of open-pit mining of minerals. © 1987 Plenum Publishing Corporation.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT MINING AND ITS MAIN ENGINEERING GEOLOGY PROBLEMS IN CHINA.
entry.dc:creator: Yao Baokui
entry.prism:publicationName: Yu Se Chin Shu Nonferrous Metals
entry.dc:description: Problems of deformation and failure of the slopes of open-pit mines are abecoming more serious in China. The engineering geology problems of the open mine mainly include: the geostress condition, which has an overall control over the stability of slopes of the open pit, especially the regional geological tectonic stress field; properties of the complex rock mass constructin and the construction of medium complexity of the rock formation associaton; open mining problems of moving rock masses which are affected by underground mining and open mining problems in karst rock masses; and the underground water problem, which evidently affects the stability of slopes of th eopen pit.

entry.dc:title: HINDUSTAN COPPER LIMITED: INDIA'S COPPER PRODUCER.
entry.dc:creator: White L.
entry.dc:description: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL), a Government of India enterprise and the nation's only producer of refined copper, operates three divisions: the Malanjkhand open-pit mine in Madhya Pradesh, the Indian Copper Complex (ICC) in Bihar, and the Khetri Copper Complex (KCC) in Rajasthan. Corporate headquarters is in Calcutta. Current copper reserves in India stand at 566 million mt in 74 deposits at an average grade of 1. 1% Cu. Estimates for Malanjkhand approach 1 billion mt of 0. 84% Cu. A working group in the Ministry of Mines, including HCL representation, formulates policy for management of these resources. Future investment is expected to focus on low cost production, and for that reason, Malanjkhand, with large reserves accessible to open-pit mining, is expected to attract the most attention.

entry.dc:title: CONTINUOUS EQUIPMENT: AN IMPORTANT TREND.
entry.dc:creator: Krumrey A.
entry.dc:description: Modern open-pit mining is characterized by ever greater volumes of material, and operation at ever greater depths. The limits of mining economy are thus shifted to increasingly less favorable overburden-to-mineral ratios so that open-pit technology becomes primarily a matter of overburden stripping while extraction of the pay mineral is a secondary consideration. The continuous method was developed in Germany, with bucketwheel excavators for mining, conveyors for onward transport, and boom stackers for overburden dumping.

entry.dc:title: MODERN OPEN-PIT MINING TECHNOLOGY.
entry.dc:creator: Ringleff H.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes two types of opencast mining technologies, which have been developed for more efficiency and reliability with regard to continuous bulk material handling. The conceptual design of a phosphate mining system is a combination of continuous bucket wheel operation, dragline strip mining, reclaiming by means of bucketwheel, and pumping the phosphate slurry in pipelines. Shiftable and mobile crushing units are special opencast systems used for hard rock formations.

entry.dc:title: Characteristics and mechanisms for the formation of structurally thickened coal deposits, southeastern Canadian Cordillera.
entry.dc:creator: Bustin R.M.
entry.prism:publicationName: 9e Congres International De Stratigraphie Et De Geologie Du Carbonifere Washington Et Champaign Urbana 1979 Compte Rendu Vol 4
entry.dc:description: Structural thickening of coal seams of the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous Kootenay Formation in the southeastern Canadian Cordillera enables open-pit mining of otherwise marginally economic deposits. In some areas, coal seams are structurally thickened by as much as an order of magnitude in response to thrust faulting, normal faulting, and folding. Predicting the distribution of structurally thickened coal requires a closely spaced drilling program, a well-planned trenching program, and an understanding of the structural style of the coal measures. -from Author

entry.dc:title: IN-PIT CRUSHING AND TROLLEY-ASSISTED TRUCK HAULAGE IN HARD ROCK OPEN-PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Mueller-Roden H.
entry.dc:description: The International Conference on 'The Planning and Operation of Open Pit and Strip Mines', organized by the University of Pretoria, the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, and the University's Mining Alumni Society, was held at the University of Pretoria Campus from April 9 to 13, 1984. The conference consisted of four parts, of which one dealt with new developments in open-pit mining, such as in-pit crushing, trolley-assisted truck haulage, and computer applications. This article presents a critical discussion on the experience gained from that conference and a visit to several mines in the Republic of South Africa.

entry.dc:title: Seismic hazard and risk in open-pit mining.
entry.dc:creator: Skipp B.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: Even with an elaborate hazard study the confidence that can be assigned to the estimate of the hazard at a particular location will never be very high. In mining operations this may impose expensive and unwarranted demand on a system that may need to work near to failure. With the seismic hazard evaluation techniques that are now available and where a first guess puts the intensity of the design earthquake at >VIII the evaluation of the hazard to be used in dynamic mine slope or dam design should be at least to the standard of the second level identified above, commensurate with the static pit slope design method. If the pit slope is to be designed with the aid of advanced numerical techniques-in particular, with probabilistic analyses-the hazard study should be of a commensurate nature.-from Author

entry.dc:title: MAMUT MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Fumoto N.
entry.dc:description: The Mamut mine which is the first porphyry copper type mine in Malaysia started its open-pit mining in May 1975. The mine is managed by Overseas Mineral Resources Development (OMRD) Sabah Bhd, a joint venture company organized by and between Malaysia and Japan. To support this project, Mamut Mines Development Co. , Ltd. (a consortium of seven major japanese non-ferrous mining and metallurgical firms), was established in Japan, and has been engaged in sales of concentrates as well as offering funds and technology assistance. The Mamut mining operation had to adopt the multi-stage narrow bench system under such situations as (1) steep topography, (2) the ore deposit being incised beneath a high hill, (3) necessity of blending the various kinds of crude ore, (4) much rainfall, (5) reduced amount of pre-stripping due to depressed initial costs and so forth. As a result, the operation needed small and medium mining equipments which had high mobility. The actual work was carried out mainly by combining wheel loaders and 40T-45T dump trucks. The various difficult problems encountered at the initial stage were overcome, and the current operation is in good progress on 500 th. T/month ore and 610 th. T/month waste basis.

entry.dc:title: INCREASING PRODUCTION WITH LOADERS AND TRUCKS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Efficient cycle time in loaders and trucks can mean increased production for any open-pit mining operation. The article gives costs and production capacities for various shovel/truck fleet sizes.

entry.dc:title: Policy analysis model for open-pit mining enterprises.
entry.dc:creator: Coyle R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: Apparently good policies at one level must not conflict with those at another. Analysis of the model shows that well-designed management policies can produce noticeable improvements in economic performance. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION OF U3O8 BEGINS AT KEY LAKE.
entry.dc:creator: Todd J.
entry.dc:description: The start-up process at Key Lake Mining Corp's (KLMC) uranium mine and mill in the Athabasca sandstone basin, 640 km north of Saskatoon, Sask. , Canada is briefly described. Key Lake ore is excavated by open-pit mining. The ore is crushed in a gyratory unit and further broken by impact crushing. Grinding is carried out by ball milling. A primary leach takes place in four downstream pachucas with the assistance of sulfuric acid and air.

entry.dc:title: Environmental Problems during Blasting Operations in Open-pit Mining and Quarrying - Possibilities of Reducing These Problems.
entry.dc:creator: Wild H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The author investigated measures to avoid or reduce blasting vibrations. Such measures include proper charge sizing of the drillhole diameter, use of detonators with short time intervals, breakdown of the charge into smaller portions, proper wall height, firing method, and avoiding mud caps in block holing.
